r.정치 구도: A federal parliamentary system led by the chancellor, with the president in a ceremonial role. Seats are allocated by vote share, so a single party rarely wins a majority and governments are always coalitions. The Christian Democratic Union and the Social Democrats are the two long-standing pillars, and the Greens and the Free Democrats have also joined coalitions. As the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has grown, how other parties form coalitions has become a big issue. The 16 states have strong powers, and the Bundesrat, made up of state governments, influences legislation.

t.why: Europe's largest economy and the center of the EU and the eurozone, and a member of NATO and the G7. It grew on exports of cars, machinery and chemicals, but it relied heavily on Russian gas, and when energy prices jumped after the war its manufacturing was shaken. It shut down its last nuclear plants in 2023. When Germany's economy weakens, growth across Europe falls with it. Since the war in Ukraine it has sharply raised defense spending and provides large-scale military aid to Ukraine.
t.rel: The EU's largest economy and, with France, the center of European integration. It relied on Russian gas, cut it off after the war in Ukraine, and is sharply raising defense spending.
t.korea: The two first established relations with the 1883 Korea-Germany treaty. In the 1960s Korean miners and nurses went to work in West Germany. Korea competes with Germany in cars and chemicals while buying its machinery and materials. Having ended its division first, Germany's reunification costs and process are often compared in Korea.
t.know: Many stretches of Germany's autobahn still have no speed limit.
etext: It is globally competitive in cars, machinery, chemicals and electrical equipment. Many small and midsize manufacturers lead the world in their niches, earning the name 'hidden champions'. Its vocational system, which combines on-the-job training with work, produces skilled workers.
It sells a large share of what it makes abroad, running a very large trade surplus. China has gone from big customer to competitor.

Energy prices rose when cheap Russian gas was cut off, and it is losing ground to Chinese makers in the shift to electric vehicles. It is criticized for slow digital infrastructure and administration. It has now begun large investments in defense and infrastructure.
